'''Jean Charlotte Spencer''' (later '''Lang''', born 10 June 1940) is a New Zealand Olympic gymnast. Born in the United Kingdom, she now lives in Australia.

==Private life==
Spencer was born in 1940 in [[Woodford, London|Woodford]], now [[Greater London]], Great Britain, but part of [[Essex]] at the time of her birth.<ref name="SR Spencer">{{Cite sports-reference |title = Jean Spencer |url = https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/sp/jean-spencer-1.html |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200418043023/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/sp/jean-spencer-1.html |url-status = dead |archive-date = 18 April 2020 |access-date = 2 September 2017 }}</ref> She received her secondary education at [[Epsom Girls' Grammar School]] in [[Auckland]], New Zealand, where she was [[Dux#Education|dux]]. She attended [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]] and graduated [[Master of Science]] with Honours in physics in 1964.<ref name="Physics prize">{{cite press release |date=4 November 2013 |title=Physics prize promises positive future |url=http://www.eggs.school.nz/uploaded/file/Media%20Release%2004%2011%202013%20-%20Physics%20prize%20promises%20positive%20future.pdf |location=Auckland |publisher=[[Epsom Girls' Grammar School]] |access-date=2 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190120080828/http://www.eggs.school.nz/uploaded/file/Media%20Release%2004%2011%202013%20-%20Physics%20prize%20promises%20positive%20future.pdf |archive-date=20 January 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She later moved to Australia.<ref name="Physics prize" /> In 2013, Lang and another Epsom Girls' Grammar School alumna established an annual prize for excellence in physics so that the recipients can enrol at a university to study physics or engineering.<ref name="Physics prize" />

==Gymnastics career==
Spencer represented her country at the [[New Zealand at the 1964 Summer Olympics|1964 Summer Olympics]] in [[Tokyo]], Japan, in gymnastics. In the [[Gymnastics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Women's vault|vault]], she came 76th. In the [[Gymnastics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Women's floor exercise|floor exercise]], she was 81st. On the [[Gymnastics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Women's uneven bars|uneven bars]], she came 75th. On the [[Gymnastics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Women's balance beam|balance beam]], she was 79th. In the [[Gymnastics at the 1964 Summer Olympics – Women's individual all-around|Women's individual all-around]], she was ranked 78th of 86 competitors.<ref name="SR Spencer" /> She is listed as New Zealand Olympic competitor number 200.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jean Lang |url= https://olympic.org.nz/athletes/jean-lang |publisher=[[New Zealand Olympic Committee]] |access-date=2 September 2017}}</ref> It would be 20 years—1984— before the next New Zealand gymnast, [[Tanya Moss]], would represent the country at another [[New Zealand at the 1984 Summer Olympics|Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/olympics/81900070/solitary-kiwi-gymnast-at-los-angeles-olympics-rapt-for-riobound-courtney-mcgregor |title=Solitary Kiwi gymnast at Los Angeles Olympics rapt for Rio-bound Courtney McGregor | work=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |date=8 July 2016 |access-date=19 May 2017 | first=Chris | last=Barclay}}</ref>

Lang was later on the national committee of the [[Gymnastics Australia|Australian Gymnastic Federation]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2002 Annual Report |url= https://www.gymnastics.org.au/images/national/About_Us/Annual_reports/2002_Annual_Report_Web.pdf |publisher=[[Gymnastics Australia]] |access-date=1 September 2017 |page=19 |date=2003}}</ref> She was the co-ordinator for elite gymnasts in [[New South Wales]] for the NSW Gymnastic Association and a judge at gymnastics competitions.<ref>{{cite web|date=2008|title=Gymnastics New South Wales 2007 Annual Report|url=http://www.gymnsw.org.au/images/nsw/.Transition_documents/Publications/GNSW_Annual_Report_2007_final_proof_LOW_RESOLUTION_2.pdf|access-date=20 May 2021|website=www.gymnsw.org.au|publisher=Gymnastics New South Wales|pages=6, 16}}</ref> She was made a life member of Gymnastics New South Wales in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=Our Life Members|url=http://www.gymnsw.org.au/NSW/About_Us/Life_Members/NSW/About/Life_Members.aspx?hkey=61683112-701e-480d-bd7a-10c6dcd85e6e|publisher=Gymnastics NSW|access-date=1 September 2017}}</ref>
